sections.title: How the deck wins
sections.text: Azula attacks every turn from turn 4 on and, while she attacks, copies every spell you cast: each instant (draw, removal, tutor) is worth double. She doesn't need to connect: the copy happens on cast, so a blocker doesn't shut the engine off. The win comes in ONE protected combat: a three-card loop with her (Narset's Reversal with Turnabout, Storm-Kiln Artist or Frantic Search; Snap with Dualcaster Mage; Return the Favor with Storm-Kiln Artist) gives unlimited mana or casts, and Comet Storm with two kicks, copied (or Thermo-Alchemist), kills all three opponents at once. Without the loop, the same combat wins on merit: copied Turnabout, the Treasures from Big Score and the mana stored in Horizon Stone, Ozai or Electro pay for a big Comet Storm, 2X to each opponent. If Azula dies, Godo brings Helm of the Host and wins with unlimited combats without her. Realistically: a full loop by turn 6 in about 3 games out of 10; in the rest you win with copied value between turns 7 and 9.

sections.title: Mulligan
sections.text: Keep 2 to 4 lands (3 or more if there's no rock or 1- or 2-mana reducer), a play by turn 3, and at least one blue source. Almost any hand with good lands is a keep if it has Sol Ring, a Signet, Mystical Teachings, Narset, Parter of Veils or Archmage Emeritus. Azula needs {1}{U}{B}{R}: with the colors in place she comes down on turn 4 in 3 of every 4 games, and two colors from lands plus a Signet or Arcane Signet is enough. Mulligan with 0 to 1 lands, with 6 or more lands, with hands of nothing but answers, or with no blue source. Don't keep a hand just because it brings one loop piece: the tutors find them, but the hand must do something every turn. With the free mulligan, you keep in about 9 of every 10 games.

sections.title: Turn by turn
sections.text: T1: land and Sol Ring if you have it; if not, keep {U} open for Brainstorm at the end of the opponent's turn. T2: Arcane Signet, a Signet, Mind Stone or a reducer (Goblin Electromancer, Stormcatch Mentor, Nightscape Familiar); Swiftfoot Boots or Tome of Legends if you already have your mana rock; Thermo-Alchemist if nothing's better. T3: Azula if you have four mana and all three colors; if not, Frostcliff Siege (Temur), Narset, Propaganda or Chromatic Lantern. T4: Azula, or the first attack: copied Mystical Teachings is the best play in the window, then Big Score, Thrill of Possibility or Thirst for Knowledge. T5: Archmage Emeritus or Storm-Kiln Artist with a counterspell open. T6 to T9: the winning turn if you have the loop and the protection; if not, Torrential Gearhulk in the window, copied Comet Storm, Helm of the Host on Azula, or Godo if they killed her. At the end of each opponent's turn, spend the leftover mana on Fact or Fiction, Pull from Tomorrow or Thirst for Knowledge.

sections.title: When to cast Azula
sections.text: Cast her as soon as you can attack early and protect her. Ideally, Swiftfoot Boots or Frostcliff Siege in Temur is already in play, so she attacks the same turn; if not, cast her with {U} open (Swan Song, Octopus Form) or with Deflecting Swat in hand, which is free once she's on the battlefield. Nightscape Familiar brings her cost down to {U}{B}{R}. Against a table with several removal spells open and nothing of yours to protect her, wait a turn and play an engine (Narset, Tome of Legends, Frostcliff Siege). If they kill her, recasting her costs {2} more each time; with Boots, Temur Siege, Hidden Footblade or Expedite she still attacks that turn. Against a wipe or a removal spell you can't counter, Snap or Venser return her to your hand in response: from hand she costs 4, with no tax.

sections.title: When to attack and when to wait
sections.text: Attack with Azula every turn you have 2 or more instants and the mana to pay for them; firebending gives you {R}{R} until end of combat, and Fire Nation Palace activated on her before attacking adds {R}{R}{R}{R}. Cast your spells after blockers are declared: removal kills the blocker and the copy hits another creature, and Hidden Footblade gives her first strike. Attack the opponent who isn't blocking; if an opponent blocks with power 4 or more, Champion's Helm makes her 6/6, Rogue's Passage ({4}) makes her unblockable, or removal after the block solves it. Only spells you cast while she attacks get copied: instants and flash cards (Dualcaster Mage, Torrential Gearhulk, Venser, Amphibian Downpour, Hidden Footblade). Sorceries are copied only if they're cast for free in the window, which Electrodominance allows. Wait if you have nothing to copy and a blocker kills her, or if the counterattack would kill you without Propaganda or blockers (for example Thermo-Alchemist or Nightscape Familiar). Never show a lethal threat one turn before you can protect her.

sections.title: Tutors and what to look for
sections.text: Mystical Teachings: cast it during Azula's combat and the copy searches for another card, so you bring back the two missing pieces (Narset's Reversal and Turnabout), or one piece and a counterspell, or Torrential Gearhulk; its flashback ({5}{B}) in the window is also copied. Solve the Equation is a sorcery: in your main phase, before attacking, fetch the missing loop piece or Comet Storm, and leave mana for combat. Shred Memory: its transmute ({1}{B}{B}, as a sorcery) searches for a card with mana value 2; in the library, Comet Storm and Electrodominance count as 2 (X = 0), same as Narset's Reversal, Snap, Return the Favor, Swiftfoot Boots, Thermo-Alchemist and Glamdring. Godo puts Helm of the Host onto the battlefield, or Swiftfoot Boots if Azula only needs protection. Order: first the piece you don't have; with the full loop, search for protection (Negate, Deflecting Swat) or the finisher.

sections.title: Graveyard
sections.text: There's no reanimation: the graveyard serves Torrential Gearhulk (it casts an instant from there for free) and Mystical Teachings' flashback. The best instants to put there: Turnabout and Frantic Search (the Gearhulk comes out free and also gives you mana), Mystical Teachings, Fact or Fiction, Big Score (cast for free, it still makes you discard), a removal spell or a counterspell. Never discard Comet Storm, Electrodominance or Pull from Tomorrow thinking of the Gearhulk: for free they have X = 0. Thrill of Possibility, Big Score, Frantic Search and Thirst for Knowledge make you discard: discard spare lands, late rocks or an instant the Gearhulk wants. Kolaghan's Command returns a dead creature to hand (Dualcaster Mage, Storm-Kiln Artist, Archmage Emeritus). Shred Memory is your only graveyard hate: if you don't need it as a tutor, keep it for a reanimator.

sections.title: What to protect against
sections.text: 1) Removal on Azula during her attack, the biggest risk: equip Swiftfoot Boots or Champion's Helm before attacking, and on the stack use Deflecting Swat (free), Redirect Lightning, Return the Favor (it changes the target, abilities included) or Narset's Reversal (it returns the removal spell to its owner's hand and you keep a copy). 2) Counterspells on the key piece: cast the cheapest piece first as bait, and keep {U} and Deflecting Swat open; a Swat aimed at a counterspell can make it target the Swat itself, and the counterspell fizzles. 3) Board wipes: answer with Swan Song, Negate or Mana Leak; Octopus Form for single-target removal; or Snap or Venser return Azula to your hand. Boots, Frostcliff Siege and equipment stay: you recast her with haste. 4) A rival combo before turn 6: four counterspells, Narset's Reversal, Venser (it returns a creature spell or a commander to hand) and instant-speed removal. 5) Effects that allow only sorcery speed, or one spell per turn: remove them with Chaos Warp, Kolaghan's Command or Aether Gale before the winning turn. 6) Your life and your library: pain lands and Redirect Lightning paid with life add up, and Archmage Emeritus forces you to draw in the loops.

sections.title: Removal priorities
sections.text: One-for-one removal does little in a four-player pod: cast it while Azula attacks and the copy takes a second target (same mode, another target). Order: 1) whatever kills or blocks Azula well that turn; 2) combo pieces and opponents' card-advantage engines; 3) the commander that threatens the most. Imprisoned in the Moon and Amphibian Downpour shut down a commander without sending it to the command zone; Terminate, Bitter Triumph, Heartless Act and Chaos Warp only send it back there. Heartless Act doesn't kill creatures with counters; Bitter Triumph kills any creature or planeswalker, and Azula's copy doesn't pay the additional cost: save Bitter Triumph for what Heartless Act can't reach. Kolaghan's Command is your answer to artifacts (two with Azula's copy); Chaos Warp is the only instant-speed answer to enchantments and lands. Don't spend removal on valuable creatures that don't threaten you: Snap and Venser are enough for tempo.

sections.title: When to clear the board
sections.text: Day of Black Sun ({X}{B}{B}) is a sorcery, and Azula doesn't copy it. At X = 0 it kills created tokens (mana value 0) for {B}{B}, but not tokens that copy a card, which keep their mana value. At X = 3 it kills everything cheap and leaves Azula, Storm-Kiln Artist, Archmage Emeritus, Venser, Godo, Ozai and the Gearhulk alive; it also kills your reducers, Thermo-Alchemist, Dualcaster Mage and Electro, so use it before casting them or once they've done their job, and never at X 4 or more while Azula is on the battlefield. Aether Gale ({3}{U}{U}) requires six nonland targets (fill them with your Treasures) and doesn't touch anything of yours you don't choose: in your main phase before the winning attack or Godo's combats, it returns blockers, commanders and stax pieces, and the tokens disappear. Electrodominance with X 5 casts it for free in the window and Azula copies it: twelve permanents. Against many small creatures that aren't tokens you have no sweeper: go over the top with Comet Storm or Thermo-Alchemist.

combos.title: Azula + Narset's Reversal + Turnabout
combos.meta: Unlimited mana · 3 cards with Azula · 6 mana on the first pass, 4+ lands (2 blue)
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Narset's Reversal and Turnabout in hand; {2}{U}{U} + {U}{U} (firebending pays the {2}); 4 or more lands, 2 of them blue (with Chromatic Lantern, any of them works). Everything in one step (declare blockers): floating mana empties when the step changes, unless you have Horizon Stone, Ozai or Electro.
Attack with Azula and, after blockers, cast Turnabout targeting yourself. Azula copies it.
Before the copy resolves, tap all your lands for mana (the mana floats). The copy resolves: you choose land and untap, and all your lands untap.
When you get priority with the original Turnabout still on the stack, cast Narset's Reversal targeting it. Azula copies Narset's Reversal: target that copy at the ORIGINAL Narset's Reversal.
The copy resolves: it creates another copy of Narset's Reversal (target Turnabout with it) and returns the original Narset's Reversal to your hand.
Tap all your lands for mana again. The new copy resolves: it copies Turnabout (you choose land and untap again) and returns Turnabout to your hand.
Repeat from casting Turnabout: each pass costs 6 and gives you twice your number of lands in mana; with 4 lands you gain 2 per pass, so the mana is unlimited.
Finish in the same step with Comet Storm (below). With Thermo-Alchemist on the battlefield, each cast untaps it: 2 damage to each opponent per pass. With Archmage Emeritus you draw 6 per pass: count your library.

combos.title: Azula + Snap + Dualcaster Mage
combos.meta: Unlimited mana and all opposing creatures to hand · 3 cards with Azula · {1}{U} + {1}{R}{R}
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Snap and Dualcaster Mage in hand; {1}{U} for Snap (firebending pays part of it) and {1}{R}{R} per pass; lands that make red.
Attack with Azula and cast Snap on an opposing creature. Azula copies it: the copy bounces another opposing creature and untaps two lands. Leave the original Snap on the stack.
With the original Snap still on the stack, cast Dualcaster Mage (flash). Azula copies it: first a Dualcaster Mage token enters.
The token copies Snap: target an opposing creature (or the token itself if none are left) and untap two lands.
The Dualcaster Mage card enters and copies Snap targeting itself: it returns to your hand and you untap two more lands.
Recast Dualcaster Mage with those lands: each pass costs 3, untaps 4 lands (+1 mana) and bounces an opposing creature. Repeat until you have the mana you want and the opposing board is empty.
Finish with Comet Storm in the same step. With Archmage Emeritus on the battlefield, each pass draws: count your library.

combos.title: Azula + Narset's Reversal + Storm-Kiln Artist
combos.meta: Unlimited Treasures and casts · 3 cards with Azula · {U}{U} + a cheap instant
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Storm-Kiln Artist already on the battlefield; Narset's Reversal in hand; a cheap instant of yours you can cast targeting something (Expedite on Azula, Brainstorm) and {U}{U}.
Attack and cast the cheap instant (Treasure for casting it, Treasure for Azula's copy). Leave the original on the stack.
Cast Narset's Reversal targeting that instant: Treasure. Azula copies it (Treasure); the copy targets the ORIGINAL Narset's Reversal.
The copy resolves: it creates another copy of Narset's Reversal (Treasure), which targets your instant, and returns the original Narset's Reversal to your hand.
When you get priority, recast Narset's Reversal paying {U}{U} with two Treasures, targeting your instant again. Each pass costs 2 Treasures and makes 3: unlimited Treasures and casts.
To stop, let the stack resolve: the first pending copy copies your instant and returns it to your hand; the rest do nothing.
Spend the Treasures on Comet Storm. With Thermo-Alchemist on the battlefield, each recast untaps it: 1 damage to each opponent per pass, which is already lethal without Comet Storm. Treasures are not lost when the step changes.

combos.title: Azula + Return the Favor + Storm-Kiln Artist
combos.meta: Unlimited Treasures (or card draw with Archmage Emeritus) · 3 cards with Azula · {R}{R}{1} + a cheap instant
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Storm-Kiln Artist (or Archmage Emeritus, to draw) on the battlefield; Return the Favor in hand; {R}{R} from firebending + {1}; a cheap instant of yours as a target.
Attack and cast the cheap instant. Leave the original on the stack.
Cast Return the Favor choosing only the copy mode (+{1}), targeting your instant: Treasure. Azula copies it; target the copy at the ORIGINAL Return the Favor.
Each copy, as it resolves, creates a new copy of the original Return the Favor (Treasure for each copy); target each new copy at the original again.
Repeat as much as you like without paying anything else: unlimited Treasures (with Archmage Emeritus, cards: stop before you empty your library).
To stop, target the last copy at your instant or at your Comet Storm already cast. Then the original resolves and copies your instant.
Spend the Treasures on Comet Storm with two kicks; Azula copies it.

combos.title: Azula + Narset's Reversal + Frantic Search
combos.meta: Digs through the library and gains +1 mana per pass · 3 cards with Azula · {2}{U} + {U}{U}
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Narset's Reversal and Frantic Search in hand; {2}{U} + {U}{U}; lands that give {U}{U}{U} per pass. Not an infinite combo: each pass draws 4 and discards 4, so your library sets the limit.
Attack and cast Frantic Search. Before Azula's copy resolves, tap your lands for mana; the copy draws 2, discards 2 and untaps 3 lands.
With the original Frantic Search on the stack, cast Narset's Reversal targeting it. Azula copies Narset's Reversal: target the copy at the ORIGINAL Narset's Reversal.
The copy creates another copy of Narset's Reversal (target Frantic Search with it) and returns Narset's Reversal to your hand; that new copy copies Frantic Search (draws 2, discards 2, untaps 3) and returns it to your hand.
Each pass costs 5 and untaps 6 lands: +1 mana (+2 with Goblin Electromancer or Stormcatch Mentor, +2 more red with Electro) and 4 new cards.
Use it to find Turnabout (and move on to the infinite loop) or Comet Storm; with Thermo-Alchemist on the battlefield it's 2 damage to each opponent per pass. Never with Archmage Emeritus on the battlefield without counting your library.

combos.title: Copied Comet Storm (tight finish)
combos.meta: 2X to each opponent, 4X with Return the Favor · Azula + 1 card · X + {R}{R} + {2} for kickers
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Comet Storm in hand; X + {R}{R} + {1}{1} (firebending pays {R}{R}). Extra mana from copied Turnabout, Big Score, Horizon Stone, Ozai, Electro, Fire Nation Palace or Glamdring (which reduces the X).
Attack with Azula; wait for blocks.
Cast Comet Storm with multikicker twice: the three opponents as targets and the biggest X you can.
Azula copies it: the copy keeps X and the kicks; choose the same three opponents. 2X to each of them.
For more copies, with Comet Storm on the stack, cast Return the Favor in copy mode ({R}{R}{1}) targeting it: Azula also copies Return the Favor, which makes two more Comet Storms (4X to each opponent). Dualcaster Mage does the same with its token.
The math: against 40 life you need X = 20 with Azula's copy, or X = 10 with four copies. You don't need to connect: the damage isn't combat damage, and blockers don't matter.

combos.title: Copied Electrodominance
combos.meta: 2X to one target and two free casts · Azula + 1 card · X + {R}{R}
combos.text:
Needs: Azula attacking; Electrodominance in hand; X + {R}{R}; a spell in hand with mana value X or less to cast for free.
Attack with Azula and cast Electrodominance with X targeting a low-life opponent, a planeswalker or a blocker.
Azula copies it: each resolution deals X damage and lets you cast a spell from your hand with mana value X or less for free, even a sorcery or a creature without flash.
Good free casts: Turnabout (X 4; copied, it untaps your lands twice), Aether Gale (X 5; copied: twelve permanents), Torrential Gearhulk or Godo (X 6). Those spells are copied too, because Azula is still attacking.
Never cast Comet Storm or Pull from Tomorrow for free: they would have X = 0. Kill one opponent (2X) and keep Comet Storm for the other two.

combos.title: Godo + Helm of the Host
combos.meta: Unlimited combats without Azula · 2 cards · {5}{R}, then {5} to equip
combos.text:
Needs: Godo, Bandit Warlord (it fetches Helm of the Host from the library); {5}{R} on one turn and {5} to equip; Godo must survive until your next main phase (or have haste). It doesn't need Azula: it's the route for when she has died.
Cast Godo: when it enters, search for Helm of the Host and put it onto the battlefield.
In your next main phase, equip the Helm to Godo ({5}; Horizon Stone or Ozai pay for it).
At the beginning of combat, the Helm creates a non-legendary Godo token with haste; its entry can search for another Equipment (Swiftfoot Boots, Champion's Helm).
Attack with Godo and the token: the first attack of each one in the turn untaps it and adds an additional combat phase.
At the start of each new combat, the Helm creates another hasty token: unlimited combats and a growing army. Spread the attacks toward opponents without solid blockers; Aether Gale or Turnabout (tapping their creatures) clear the way first.
Its weak point: artifact removal on the Helm or a board wipe; keep a counterspell ready.

cards.Fire Lord Azula: Your engine: she only needs to be attacking, not connecting. Attack each turn with 2 or more instants in hand and cast them after blockers are declared; firebending covers {R}{R} of their cost. In the window, prioritize what gains the most from the copy: tutors (Mystical Teachings), card draw (Big Score, Thirst for Knowledge), removal and the loop pieces; sorceries are not copied.
cards.Sol Ring: Always turn 1: with the extra mana, Azula comes down on turn 3 if you have the colors. Late, it's just colorless mana for Comet Storm's X.
cards.Arcane Signet: Turn-2 rock that makes any of the three colors: it fixes Azula's {U}{B}{R} for turn 3. Cast it before Mind Stone if you're missing a color.
cards.Everflowing Chalice: Turn 2 with one counter; late, with two or three counters, for Comet Storm's X or Pull from Tomorrow. If it arrives late and there's no spare mana, it's the artifact you discard to Thirst for Knowledge.
cards.Izzet Signet: Turn 2: converts one mana into {U}{R}. Inside the Turnabout loop, choosing artifacts on one resolution untaps it along with your other rocks, getting the red for Comet Storm.
cards.Dimir Signet: Turn 2: converts one mana into {U}{B}, the double blue for Narset's Reversal and Turnabout and the black for Azula. Like Izzet Signet, Turnabout choosing artifacts untaps it.
cards.Mind Stone: Turn 2 if there's no Signet. Late, crack it ({1}, sacrifice) for a card at the end of an opponent's turn, or discard it to Thirst for Knowledge if it's still in hand.
cards.Bender's Waterskin: Turn 3 if you have no 2-mana rock. It untaps on each opponent's turn: one mana of any color for Mana Leak, Octopus Form, Mystical Teachings or Venser without tapping your lands.
cards.Goblin Electromancer: Turn 2. Every instant costs {1} less: Frantic Search drops to {1}{U}, Big Score to {2}{R}, and Return the Favor's copy mode costs {R}{R}, so loops with Narset's Reversal gain more mana. It doesn't reduce Narset's Reversal ({U}{U}). It's removal bait: don't risk it in blocks.
cards.Stormcatch Mentor: Turn 2: a cost reducer like Goblin Electromancer, but with haste and prowess. Attack alongside Azula at the opponent with no blockers, and it grows with each spell you cast (copies don't count).
cards.Nightscape Familiar: Turn 2: Azula costs {U}{B}{R}, and almost all your blue or red spells cost {1} less. While Azula attacks, keep it home as a blocker: it regenerates for {1}{B}.
cards.Snap: Save it for the window: copied, it bounces two blockers and untaps four lands, so it effectively costs nothing or gives you mana. With Dualcaster Mage it's a loop (see combos). On defense, return Azula to your hand in response to a removal spell or a board wipe: you recast her for 4 with no tax.
cards.Narset's Reversal: The center of the loops: with Azula attacking, her copy targets the original Narset's Reversal (see the combos with Turnabout, Storm-Kiln Artist and Frantic Search). Alone it's protection: against removal on Azula, it returns that removal spell to its owner's hand and you keep a copy; or you keep a copy of the best tutor or draw spell an opponent casts. Don't spend it on something minor if the loop is close.
cards.Frantic Search: In the window it pays for itself: copied, it untaps six lands at a cost of 3 and lets you look at four cards (twice: draw 2 and discard 2). Discard spells you won't cast, spare lands or an instant for the Gearhulk. With Narset's Reversal, dig toward Turnabout or Comet Storm. In the graveyard it's the Gearhulk's best target.
cards.Turnabout: Bad early: save it for Azula's combat. Copied, it untaps all your lands twice (with 8 lands, 16 mana) for a big Comet Storm; tap your lands for mana before each copy resolves. With Narset's Reversal it's unlimited mana. In your main phase it can also tap an opponent's creatures before you attack.
cards.Dualcaster Mage: Flash: cast it in the window, targeting your best instant; Azula copies it and the token also copies, so that's two more copies (Comet Storm, Mystical Teachings, Big Score). With Snap it's a mana loop. Outside combat, copy an opponent's tutor, removal or draw in response.
cards.Storm-Kiln Artist: Cast it a turn before the big attack, with a counterspell open: in the window each instant gives two Treasures (cast and copy). With Narset's Reversal or Return the Favor it's unlimited Treasures. Save the Treasures for the next window.
cards.Archmage Emeritus: Cast it with a counterspell open (turn 5 or 6): in the window each instant draws you two, and the copies of Narset's Reversal, Return the Favor and Dualcaster Mage draw too. The draw is mandatory: in the loops, count your library (with Turnabout it's six cards per pass).
cards.Thermo-Alchemist: Turn 2 as a blocker and as a clock: tap it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you for 1 damage to each opponent. It untaps each time you cast an instant (copies don't count): in any loop it's the way to kill the table without Comet Storm. It must be under your control since the start of your turn to use {T}.
cards.Electro, Assaulting Battery: Turn 3 or 4 if Azula doesn't come down. Each instant gives you {R}, and the red isn't lost between steps or turns: save firebending and spare mana for your main phase or the next combat. If it's about to die or get removed, pay X with that saved red to finish off a player.
cards.Horizon Stone: Tested by the deck owner: with it no mana is lost; it stays colorless. Save the firebending, the copied Turnabout and the mana from each turn's end for Comet Storm's X or Pull from Tomorrow, the Helm's equip, or Godo. Cast it when you have spare mana (turn 6 or later), never instead of Azula.
cards.Comet Storm: Your finisher: with two kicks it targets all three opponents and Azula copies it (2X to each, the X is kept); Return the Favor or Dualcaster Mage add copies. Early, with X 2 or 3, the copy clears blockers. Never cast it with the Gearhulk (free, so X = 0).
cards.Electrodominance: In the window: X damage and, on each resolution, you cast for free a spell from your hand with mana value X or less, even a sorcery or a creature: Turnabout (X 4), Aether Gale (X 5), Torrential Gearhulk or Godo (X 6), and those get copied too. Outside the window, at the end of an opponent's turn, it lets you cast a sorcery at instant speed.
cards.Helm of the Host: Bad early. On Azula, each combat creates a non-legendary Azula token with haste: with two Azulas attacking, each spell is copied twice. On Godo it means unlimited combats (see combos). Godo brings it in; pay the {5} equip with Horizon Stone or Ozai.
cards.Godo, Bandit Warlord: Turn 6 or later: when it enters, it puts Helm of the Host onto the battlefield (or Swiftfoot Boots, if that's what's missing). It's the route that doesn't need Azula: the Helm on Godo gives unlimited combats the next turn. With Azula attacking, Electrodominance with X 6 casts it for free; the copy also searches for an Equipment, and then you keep just one Godo because of the legend rule.
cards.Ozai, the Phoenix King: Bad early. Cast it in your main phase before attacking: it has haste and firebending 4, attacks right away and gives you {R}{R}{R}{R}; with Azula that's six red per combat. Mana you don't spend stays red, and with six or more unspent it has flying and indestructible: save it for Comet Storm. Attack the opponent with the fewest blockers: with trample, a small block doesn't stop it.
cards.Mystical Teachings: Cast it in the window: the copy searches for another card, so you bring back the two missing pieces (Narset's Reversal and Turnabout), one piece and a counterspell, or Torrential Gearhulk. Outside combat, cast it at the end of an opponent's turn. Its flashback ({5}{B}) in the window is also copied.
cards.Solve the Equation: Sorcery: not copied. Use it in your main phase before attacking to find the missing loop piece or Comet Storm, leaving mana for combat. With the loop already in hand, search for Negate or Deflecting Swat to protect it.
cards.Narset, Parter of Veils: Game Changer. Turn 3 if Azula doesn't come down: two uses of -2 look at eight cards for a piece, a tutor or a counterspell. Its static ability only restrains opponents: punish the one who draws the most first. Protect her with Propaganda and blockers.
cards.Brainstorm: At the end of an opponent's turn, or copied in the window (twice: draw 3, put back 2). Put back on top what you won't cast soon, and use it before a shuffle (Mystical Teachings, Solve the Equation, Godo, Shred Memory) so those cards get shuffled away.
cards.Thirst for Knowledge: At the end of an opponent's turn it draws 3; in the window it draws 6. Discard a spare artifact (a late rock, Everflowing Chalice, Helm of the Host without Godo) or two instants the Gearhulk wants in the graveyard.
cards.Glamdring, Foe-hammer // Gleam of Death: First Gleam of Death ({3}{U}, sorcery in your main phase): mill six and keep every instant and sorcery among them. Then cast Glamdring from exile and equip it to Azula: your instants cost {4} less (Turnabout {U}{U}, Big Score {R}, Mystical Teachings {U} and Comet Storm's X), {6} with Champion's Helm. That way every loop with Narset's Reversal gains much more mana.
cards.Big Score: Cast it in the window: you discard once, and the copy doesn't ask for a discard, so you draw 4 and create 4 Treasures that pay for the rest of combat or feed Storm-Kiln Artist. Discard a spare land or an instant for the Gearhulk. Without Azula, cast it at the end of the turn of the opponent before you.
cards.Thrill of Possibility: In the window: discard one card, draw four. Outside combat it only filters: cast it at the end of an opponent's turn only if you have a dead card in hand.
cards.Fact or Fiction: At the end of the turn of the opponent before you, or copied in the window (two five-card piles). The pile you don't take goes to the graveyard: good fuel for the Gearhulk.
cards.Pull from Tomorrow: Bad early. At the end of the turn of the opponent before you, with all your mana as X. Copied in the window it draws 2X; with Horizon Stone or Ozai saving mana, it's a full reload. Never with the Gearhulk (X = 0).
cards.Venser, Shaper Savant: Flash: your answer to any spell, including a creature spell or a commander on the stack (it returns that spell to its owner's hand). In the window it's copied: two bounces of blockers or commanders; then you keep one Venser because of the legend rule. It also returns Azula to your hand against a board wipe, and on an opponent's turn it's a flash blocker.
cards.Torrential Gearhulk: Cast it in the window with two instants in your graveyard: Azula copies it, each Gearhulk casts an instant for free from the graveyard, and those get copied too. Best targets: Turnabout and Frantic Search (they return the mana to you), Mystical Teachings, Fact or Fiction, Big Score; it recovers a loop piece that was spent or countered. On an opponent's turn it's a 5/6 with flash that recasts a counterspell or removal spell. Never with Comet Storm, Electrodominance or Pull from Tomorrow (X = 0).
cards.Return the Favor: {R}{R}, which firebending pays. In the window, with copy mode, aim it at Comet Storm (Azula copies it: two more Comet Storms), or with Storm-Kiln Artist or Archmage Emeritus aim its copy at the original for the loop. On defense, the change-target mode diverts a removal spell or an ability aimed at Azula. It also copies triggers: firebending (+{R}{R}), Godo's extra combat, the Helm's token.
cards.Expedite: {R}: haste for a recast Azula, Godo or the Gearhulk, and draw a card. In the window it's cheap fuel: copied, it draws two. If there are no Boots or Siege, save it for the Azula who comes back.
cards.Heartless Act: Two mana for almost any creature without counters; against creatures with counters, the other mode removes up to three. Best in the window after blockers: the copy kills another one.
cards.Tome of Legends: Turn 2: gains a page each time Azula enters or attacks. Draw for {1} at the end of an opponent's turn, or in combat paying with firebending. It's constant card draw that works even without a window; without Azula it runs out of pages.
cards.Terminate: Destroys any creature; it can't be regenerated. Save it for a commander or a big blocker; in the window it kills the blocker and its copy kills another creature.
cards.Imprisoned in the Moon: Aura without flash: not copied. In your main phase, cast it on the commander the table fears most: it becomes a land on the battlefield, and its owner can't return it to the command zone. It also works against a planeswalker or a utility land.
cards.Chaos Warp: Your instant-speed answer to any permanent: enchantment, land, planeswalker or a stax piece. A commander goes back to the command zone; against that, prefer Imprisoned in the Moon. Its owner reveals another card that may enter: use it on big threats.
cards.Kolaghan's Command: Choose two modes; the copy in the window repeats the same modes with other targets: destroy two artifacts and deal 2 damage to two targets, or return two creatures from your graveyard to hand (Dualcaster Mage, Storm-Kiln Artist). Outside the window, it kills a pinger or a mana creature and makes a player discard.
cards.Swan Song: {U}: counters a board wipe, an instant removal spell or a counterspell aimed at your key piece. The spell's owner gets a 2/2 flying Bird: count it as a new blocker or attacker.
cards.Negate: Counters any noncreature spell: board wipes, removal, combos. Save it for the winning turn, or for the wipe that arrives when Azula is already equipped.
cards.Swiftfoot Boots: Turn 2 or 3, before Azula: that way she comes down, equips for {1} and attacks that same turn with hexproof. They stay on the battlefield after a wipe, ready for the recast Azula.
cards.Champion's Helm: On Azula: 6/6 with hexproof (she's legendary), it wins almost every block. With Glamdring her instants cost {6} less. Use it when she already has haste, or instead of Boots against tables with big creatures.
cards.Frostcliff Siege: Turn 3 if you have no rock. Temur when Azula has no Boots or has just come back: haste with no equip cost, +1/+0 and trample for everyone. Jeskai when she already has Boots: a card each turn you hit the opponent who doesn't block. It survives board wipes.
cards.Hidden Footblade: {R} with flash: after blockers, cast it on Azula, and she gains first strike: she kills the blocker before taking damage. In the window it gets copied and the copy goes on another creature of yours. Outside that, haste for a recast Azula.
cards.Chromatic Lantern: Turn 3 instead of another rock when colors are missing: all your lands make any color, including filter lands and Rogue's Passage. In the Turnabout loop, every untapped land pays {U}{U} or {R}{R} with no trouble.
cards.Deflecting Swat: Free while Azula is on the battlefield: it redirects removal to an opposing creature, or makes a counterspell target the Swat itself so it fizzles. It's the cheapest protection for the winning turn: don't spend it on something minor.
cards.Redirect Lightning: {R} plus {2} or 5 life: like Deflecting Swat, but only against spells or abilities with a single target. Pay life only if you're above 25; redirect the removal to the leader's best blocker.
cards.Mana Leak: The only cheap counterspell that stops a creature spell or a commander. Best from turn 2 to 6, or when an opponent taps out completely; late, use it on your turn against a player with no mana open.
cards.Amphibian Downpour: Flash: cast it at the end of the window, after several spells: storm counts each spell cast earlier in the turn (opponents' too), and Azula adds another copy. Each copy turns a creature into a 1/1 Frog with no abilities: commanders shut off without going to the command zone. Alone, on an opponent's turn, it shuts down a commander.
cards.Day of Black Sun: Sorcery: Azula doesn't copy it. X = 0 for {B}{B} kills created tokens; X = 3 kills everything cheap and leaves Azula, Storm-Kiln Artist, Archmage Emeritus, Venser and Ozai alive. It also kills your reducers and Thermo-Alchemist: use it before casting them or once they've done their job.
cards.Aether Gale: Bad early. A five-mana sorcery that requires six nonland targets (fill them with your Treasures). In your main phase before the winning attack or Godo's combats: blockers, commanders and stax pieces go to hand, and the tokens disappear. Electrodominance with X 5 casts it in the window, and it gets copied.
cards.Propaganda: Tested by the deck owner. Turn 3: each attacker against you costs {2}; it protects your life and Narset while Azula is tapped, and pushes attacks toward the other players.
cards.Shred Memory: Two uses. Its transmute ({1}{B}{B}, as a sorcery) searches for a card with mana value 2: Narset's Reversal, Snap, Return the Favor, Comet Storm or Electrodominance (X = 0 in the library), or Swiftfoot Boots. If you don't need it as a tutor, keep it as an instant against a reanimator; copied in the window, it clears two graveyards.
cards.Command Tower: Any of the three colors: your best first land.
cards.Exotic Orchard: Makes the colors that your opponents' lands can make; on tables with no blue or black, play other lands first.
cards.Fire Nation Palace: Enters tapped if you have no basic. Before the winning combat, activate it ({1}{R}, {T}) on Azula: firebending 4, six red when attacking.
cards.Rogue's Passage: Colorless. {4} and {T} make Azula unblockable (it secures the Frostcliff Siege card in Jeskai) or Ozai, for the final blow.
cards.Cascade Bluffs: Filter land: with another source of {U} or {R}, it makes {U}{U} or {R}{R} for Narset's Reversal, Turnabout or Comet Storm. Don't play it as your only colored land.
cards.Choked Estuary: Reveal an Island or Swamp so it enters untapped: play it early with a basic in hand.
cards.Darkwater Catacombs: Pay {1} and it makes {U}{B}: like a Signet. Not a first-turn land.
cards.Dragonskull Summit: Enters untapped if you control a Swamp or Mountain (Smoldering Marsh counts).
cards.Drowned Catacomb: Enters untapped if you control an Island or Swamp (Sunken Hollow counts).
cards.Foreboding Ruins: Reveal a Swamp or Mountain so it enters untapped.
cards.Frostboil Snarl: Reveal an Island or Mountain so it enters untapped.
cards.Shadowblood Ridge: Pay {1} and it makes {B}{R}: like a Signet. Not a first-turn land.
cards.Shivan Reef: Blue or red for 1 damage; colorless at no cost, for the X.
cards.Smoldering Marsh: Enters tapped until you control two basics: play it on turn 1 or late. It's a Swamp and a Mountain for Dragonskull Summit.
cards.Sulfur Falls: Enters untapped if you control an Island or Mountain.
cards.Sulfurous Springs: Black or red for 1 damage; colorless at no cost, for the X.
cards.Sunken Hollow: Enters tapped until you control two basics: play it on turn 1 or late. It's an Island and a Swamp for Drowned Catacomb.
cards.Sunken Ruins: Filter land: with another source of {U} or {B}, it makes {U}{U} or {B}{B}. Don't play it as your only colored land.
cards.Underground River: Blue or black for 1 damage; colorless at no cost, for the X.
cards.Island: Seven copies: the {U}{U} for Narset's Reversal, Turnabout and the Gearhulk; they also turn on the lands that check for basic types.
cards.Mountain: Six copies: the red for Comet Storm, Dualcaster Mage and Return the Favor outside combat.
cards.Swamp: Four copies: the black for Azula, removal and Day of Black Sun.
cards.Octopus Form: Your cheapest protection: keep {U} open for it when Azula attacks or when you cast a loop piece. It answers single-target removal, and untapping her leaves Azula ready to block after she attacks. With Azula attacking, the copy protects a second creature.
cards.Bitter Triumph: Instant removal for {1}{B} against any creature or planeswalker, artifact creatures included. Pay 3 life rather than discard a combo piece; with Azula attacking, the copy kills a second target without paying the additional cost.
cards.Theater of Horrors: Theater of Horrors is card draw that keeps working even if they kill Azula: each upkeep exiles a card, and you play it on your turn if an opponent lost life (an attack, Thermo-Alchemist or its own {3}{R} ability). Cast it on turn 3 or 4 and build up cards for the combo turn.
